text:
Muse (Meta) endpoint 400s on oneOf — switch tool schemas to anyOf

Symptom (observed 2027-01-18, live in-session): a streaming request to the Meta "muse" endpoint (https://api.meta.ai/v1/chat/completions) failed terminally — HTTP 400 {"error":{"code":null,"message":"'oneOf' is not permitted.","param":"parameters","type":"invalid_request_error"}}. Retries exhausted; the agent turn died. Reproduce: on the muse endpoint, run any turn whose request includes the create_plan/update_plan tools — their `steps` items schema embeds a oneOf union, and muse's OpenAI-compat layer rejects `oneOf` outright inside tool `parameters`.

Exact sites:
- src/app/tool/workflow/plan.rs:703 — create_plan steps.items.oneOf [string | {header, body}]
- src/app/tool/workflow/plan.rs:1116 — update_plan steps.items.oneOf (same shape)
- src/tool/mod.rs:1475 — test stringified_null_dropped_through_union_branches mirrors that schema (update in lockstep)
- Request path: src/provider/openai.rs:691 (the "stream request" provider_error). Walkers that must stay consistent: src/tool/mod.rs:222 and :235 (drop_stringified_nulls recurses into anyOf/oneOf/allOf) and src/provider/strict.rs:59/:87/:208 (strict-mode normalizer already walks anyOf branches).

Fix direction (user-confirmed 2027-01-18): use anyOf instead of oneOf — replace both hand-written oneOf unions with anyOf at the two plan.rs sites and mirror the change in the tool/mod.rs test schema. Semantics: these are permissive unions (a step is a string OR an object), so anyOf is the correct, looser match; oneOf's exactly-one constraint was never intended.

Acceptance criteria:
1. A search for oneOf in src/ returns only walker KEY lists (src/tool/mod.rs:235, src/provider/strict.rs:87/:208) — no emitted tool schema carries it.
2. Regression test: build the create_plan (and update_plan) tool schema and assert the serialized `parameters` contain "anyOf" and no "oneOf".
3. The strict-mode and drop_stringified_nulls tests still pass (anyOf flows through both walkers unchanged).
4. cargo test green (workspace).
5. Manual: a muse turn including create_plan/update_plan no longer 400s.

Pointers: error-string precedent src/error.rs:388-429 (provider_error shape); failure observed in the job-3b session (2027-01-18 harness note).
plan_title: Muse (Meta) 400 fix: plan tool schemas oneOf → anyOf

text:
Close the 340K proxy-cache cliff leak (R20a-c)

Problem (2027-01-09 cache round 5, HIGH): post-R12, 47 requests still crossed the ~340K litellm proxy cache ceiling at 16.3% hit (340-400K bucket: 83.7% resets; daily maxP reaches 408,956). R13 (fill_rate 0.3 + the 340K ceiling minus a 32,768 margin → effective trigger ~300K on 1M-window GLM endpoints) did NOT prevent over-cliff prompts.

Root cause (three stacked gaps, code-verified):
1. Rule-4 skip: when the conversation ends in an open tool loop spanning back to messages[1] (a long single-turn tool run — exactly where context grows fastest), summary_cut_index retreats the cut to the loop start and summarize returns messages UNCHANGED (src/agent/context.rs:262-264, 336-338, 437-485); maybe_compact falls through and the request is sent at full size.
2. No send-gate: when compaction runs but cannot shrink below the threshold, the code explicitly continues (src/agent/turn.rs:1743-1750 — "Still over: the kept-verbatim tail dominates..."); the 5-attempt budget aborts only on the 5th attempt, so up to 4 over-cliff requests go out per turn, and the next turn resets the budget.
3. Tokenizer drift: the trigger counts cl100k BPE tokens; the provider counts GLM tokens (~10% higher on code-heavy content) — a 300K-cl100k conversation can be 330-345K provider tokens, and one iteration's tool results plus GLM reasoning echo (policy: never strip) jumps past the trigger between checks.

Fix instructions (R20, three parts):
a. Send-gate at the cliff (src/agent/turn.rs maybe_compact ~:1660-1760): when the pre-request count is still over the proxy ceiling after the compaction attempts, do NOT send the full prompt — either (i) allow under-pressure historical-reasoning stripping for GLM as a cliff-pressure exception (the under_pressure machinery exists at src/provider/openai/request.rs:54 and DeepSeek uses it; GLM's never-strip policy blocks it — src/provider/policy.rs), or (ii) fail the turn fast with an actionable error instead of burning up to 4 over-cliff requests.
b. Trigger margin for 1M-window endpoints (src/config/general.rs:334/343 defaults; src/agent/context.rs:151-163 trigger math): lower the effective trigger to ~280K (fill 0.28 for 1M windows, or ceiling 320K) so tokenizer drift plus one tool batch cannot jump past the cliff.
c. Rule-4 fast-fail signal: when summarize no-ops because the open tool loop spans the conversation AND the count is over the ceiling, return a "skipped: open loop" signal from summarize/summarize_with_interrupt (src/agent/context.rs:262-264, 336-338) so maybe_compact surfaces "context over the proxy cache ceiling inside an open tool loop — finish or interrupt the tool run" immediately instead of silently re-sending.

Acceptance: a regression test where a conversation over the ceiling inside an open tool loop fails fast (or strips under pressure) instead of sending >340K; no post-fix request_stats row exceeds the ceiling (verify via the aggregates extraction); cargo test --workspace green with the existing compaction tests updated to the new behavior.

Pointers: .coding/reviews/2026-09-09-cache-hit-5-review.md (HIGH-1, R20); .coding/analysis/cache-hit-5-aggregates.txt (A3/A4 buckets); executive summary BUG 4.

multi_edit tool + compact line-op syntax for file_edit

Every file change today costs a byte-exact `old_string` anchor plus `new_string`, one call and one approval per file. For line-targeted changes (insert at line 101, delete 202-205, replace line 102) the agent must first read the text and then echo it byte-exact as the anchor — the read and the echoed anchor are pure token overhead. User request, current session.

WHAT EXISTS
- src/tool/agent/file_edit.rs: `FileEditArgs` (line 51) has literal / regex / line-range `lines:[start,end]` (line 84, replace-only) / atomic batch `edits:[EditItem]` (line 103) / `append` (line 113) — every mode is single-file.
- Reusable pieces: `compute_diff` (line 162), `PreparedEdit` (line 150), `with_fresh_read_nudge` (line 180), the emission advisory (line 198); line endings in src/tool/agent/line_endings.rs; sandboxed writes in src/tool/agent/sandbox.rs.
- Registration: src/agent/factory.rs imports FileEditTool (line 55) and wires it in the file-tool block.
- Name-keyed gates to extend: src/agent/dispatch.rs `file_edit_redirect` (line 1293), src/agent/steering_stats.rs `should_gate_file_edit` (line 626).
- Frontend: frontend/src/components/chat/ApprovalPrompt.tsx (`isProjectScoped` line 23, `isFileEdit` line 53, single-path diff preview) and frontend/src/lib/toolCardPaths.ts (`argPaths`, `fileEditDiff` line 747, `buildPathChips`).

DIRECTION
1. Shared op engine in a new src/tool/agent/edit_ops.rs (parse + apply), used by BOTH tools: file_edit gains an `ops` field (same file), and a new src/tool/agent/multi_edit.rs takes `files:[{path, edits:[...]}]` applying every file atomically — any failing op aborts with NO write anywhere — and returns one combined diff preview.
2. Compact encoding: one STRING per line op instead of an object (the repeated JSON keys are the cost). Verb + range + first `:` + payload, split on the FIRST `:` — `i101:text` insert after line 101; `b101:text` insert before; `d202-205` delete inclusive (`d202` single, `d100-` to EOF); `r102:text` replace one line; `r100-120:text` replace a range. 1-indexed inclusive, matching the existing `lines` semantics. Multi-line payload rides JSON `\n` escapes — no extra framing. Anchor-based edits stay as EditItem objects in the SAME array, so one field carries both forms.
3. Frontend: add the new tool name to ApprovalPrompt's project-scoped switch, render a preview covering every changed file, and map its paths to chips in toolCardPaths.
4. Token budget: tool schemas are injected every turn — decide whether multi_edit sits beside file_edit or absorbs it, keep the description terse, and measure the delta.

VERIFY
- `cargo test` green and warning-free (#![deny(warnings)]).
- Per-verb unit tests; out-of-range lines (mirror file_edit.rs:2472 clamp-end / 2524 error-on-start-beyond-EOF); CRLF preservation; atomicity — a failing op leaves EVERY file byte-identical (regression test).
- Measure a 3-file change done the old way (3 anchored file_edit calls) vs the new call; record the bytes/tokens saved in the plan context.
- Sync README.md / PLAN.md tool tables if file_edit's surface changes.

text:
Laya classifier foundation: opt-in sidecar + Classifier trait

Foundation item — item 1 of a 5-item Laya integration chain; the other four (pre-prompt model routing, tool-choice steering, error/flaky-test triage, memory auto-typing) each depend on this one, so queue and land it first.

Problem: Mnemo (repo root C:/AgenticCoder/AgenticCoder, Rust/Tauri) has no fast 'System 1' classifier for cheap, calibrated decisions. Laya (https://huggingface.co/convaiinnovations/laya) is a ~33 ms calibrated text-classification model served over HTTP by laya-serve (POST /v1/systemone, Jev-compatible; Python package, Apache 2.0). Laya never generates text; it answers typed questions (choice / score / yes-no) with calibrated probabilities.

Hard requirement — opt-in only, disabled by default: when Laya is disabled or not installed, the app behaves exactly as today — no classifier calls, no startup cost, no new failure modes.

Fix direction — mirror the existing embedder pattern end to end:
- Add a Classifier trait mirroring Embedder (src/memory/embedder.rs; e.g. src/memory/classifier.rs) with a Laya HTTP backend that POSTs typed questions to /v1/systemone.
- Config-driven construction alongside build_embedder (src/provider/client_factory.rs:313): add build_classifier; disabled/absent yields a null/no-op backend (same graceful-fallback spirit as HashEmbedder) and never errors or blocks startup.
- Status via Tauri IPC like embedder_status (src-tauri/src/ipc/state.rs:323), surfaced in the Settings UI.
- Add a Laya section to the config/Settings dialog: the user can either download/install laya-serve as a sidecar or point at an already-running endpoint URL, and enable it with a toggle.

Caveat: Laya base checkpoints are near-chance zero-shot on custom tasks — every downstream classifier needs fine-tuning on Mnemo-specific labeled data before it gates any real decision; this item ships the plumbing, logging, and fine-tuning path only.

Acceptance: cargo test passes with Laya disabled and behavior is unchanged; with it enabled, a test classification round-trips end-to-end (e.g. a choice question against a stub HTTP server), and Settings shows enabled/disabled + endpoint.

Pre-prompt model routing via Laya complexity classifier

Item 2 of the 5-item Laya chain. Depends on item 1 (backlog bb54bdcc-b692-47f2-9a72-7f0692f9f7c2, 'Laya classifier foundation: opt-in sidecar + Classifier trait') — land that first; this item uses its Classifier trait.

Problem: every turn runs on the model chosen in config/Settings; there is no pre-prompt routing that sends trivial edits to a cheap model and architectural work to a capable one. Laya (~33 ms) can classify task complexity before the prompt is built. 

Before you build lets discuss how that would be configured. Suggest a configuration setup

Fix direction:
- Add a pre-prompt classification step before prompt assembly: model selection lives in src/model_resolver.rs (ModelResolver; state models at models.executing :350, models.subagent :293, models.bug_fixing :315; resolve_model_ref src/config/mod.rs:109), prompt assembly in src/agent/prompt.rs, turn loop in src/agent/turn.rs. - Confidence-gated: below a configured threshold → the current default model. Low confidence must never change model choice.
- Config: cheap model id, capable model id, threshold, enable flag (src/config/general.rs pattern). Laya disabled (item 1 off) → zero behavior change, today's selection exactly.
- Training data: historical sessions with outcomes (task text → model used → outcome). Add decision+outcome logging now. Laya base checkpoints are near-chance zero-shot on custom tasks — the router needs fine-tuning on Mnemo-specific labeled data + threshold calibration before it gates any real decision: ship plumbing + logging first, enforce only after fine-tuning.

Problem (observed live 2026-09-19, plans 995436c2 + 04a195de review rounds): an agent passing explicit JSON null for an optional string- or enum-typed tool parameter has the null arrive as the literal string "null" — breaking enum validation, triggering false mutual-exclusion errors, and silently corrupting data. Four distinct live failures this session: (1) backlog_status(status=null) → "argument has a value outside the allowed set (allowed: pending, in_flight, done, failed, cant_resolve)" — the null became "null" (the only note-update path left is a done→pending→done requeue dance); (2) update_plan(title=null, goal=null) → the plan's title and goal were REPLACED with the string "null" ("updated plan 'null' … title set, goal set") — data corruption requiring manual repair; (3) create_plan(branch=null) → "git checkout null failed: error: pathspec 'null' did not match any file(s)"; (4) file_edit(edits=[…] with old_string=null, new_string=null) → "edits is mutually exclusive with old_string" — the stringified "null" counted as Some, making batch mode unusable through the transport. Control: integer/array/boolean params (count, edits, start_line/end_line, append) pass null cleanly (dropped/absent) — the stringification is specific to string/enum-typed fields. Same transport class as backlog 3e6f7887 (spawn_agent model:null), which fixed that ONE field's symptom but not the general behavior.

Reproduce: call backlog_status with {"id": "<any done item>", "status": null, "note": "x"} → enum rejection naming "null"; or update_plan with title=null on any plan → title becomes "null".

Files/symbols: the stringification lives in the tool-call transport/argument decoding — src/provider/strict.rs (normalize_for_strict; the strict client that auto-fills omitted optional properties with null) and the Tool args deserialization (src/tool/mod.rs). Fix direction: (1) make every optional string/enum param advertise nullable (type: ["string", "null"] / enum ∪ null) so explicit null is legal end-to-end and deserializes to None — mirror the spawn_agent.model fix across the harness tool surface; (2) defense-in-depth: the argument decoder treats a literal "null" string for a nullable field as absent (same as the reviewer gate); (3) regression test per fixed field: explicit null → None, omitted → None, real value → passes through. text:
read_files empty-argument failure mode: collapse dual input forms

Problem (observed 2027-01-24, wt/mnemo): every read_files failure this session had the same shape — a well-formed read_files({files:[...]}) succeeds, then the NEXT read_files call is emitted with an empty argument object → "parameter 'files' is required". Not a schema-knowledge gap — an ambiguity the dual input forms expose.

Fix direction (priority order), in src/tool/agent/read_files.rs (tool definition + description; the path shorthand is parsed by read_files_paths in src/agent/dispatch.rs):
1. Collapse the two input forms: the schema offers path (single-path shorthand) and files (array) — two mutually-exclusive ways to say the same thing, exactly the ambiguity that produces empty calls. Make the description one line: "Always pass files (an array). There is no zero-argument form — a read_files call with no files is always an error." Highest value.
2. State the recovery rule in the tool description: "On a 'files is required' error, do NOT resend — rewrite the full call from the path(s) you meant." (The global correction only lands after two failures; this makes the first retry succeed.)
3. Add one inline example of the exact call shape: read_files({files:[{path:"a.js",start_line:10,max_lines:40}]}) — nearly free, catches the rest.
4. Consider merging read into search: search_read already returns file contents and was never fumbled this session (its required param is a plain string pattern, not an optional-array-plus-optional-string pair). Folding the batch-read into the same shape would remove the failure-prone tool from the common "read these N files" path.

Acceptance criteria: cargo test green + warning-free; description changes asserted where the tool schema is tested; if the path shorthand is removed, update read_files_paths (src/agent/dispatch.rs) + its tests.

text:
Reviewer prompts must be clean — skip the recalled-context rider for reviewer spawns

Problem (user report 2026-09-19, observed on the reviewers spawned during plan 995436c2's closing sequence): every spawned reviewer's first prompt — the `task` — now arrives with an embedded "recalled context" block (memories semantically matched to the task text). The reviewer prompt needs to be CLEAN: the reviewer protocol hands it a self-contained task, and the rider pollutes it with parent-project memories — noise at best, review bias at worst (the reviewer should judge the diff/plan, not be steered by recalled context), plus needless prompt bloat on every review.

Reproduce: spawn any role:"reviewer" agent whose task text matches existing memories (e.g. mentions "review", "diff", a file path, or a plan topic) with the memory store populated — the spawned agent's first prompt carries the recalled-context rider; visible in the reviewer's transcript/task echo.

Files/symbols: the rider lives in src/tool/agent/spawn_agent.rs `execute` — the "RECALLED CONTEXT rider" block (~lines 297-315) calling `crate::tool::steering::recalled_context_block(self.memory.as_ref(), None, &args.task, None)` and prepending the rider via `format!("{}{rider}", args.task)`. It runs for EVERY spawn with no role check. The role is already resolved earlier in `execute` (the `role` match that validates "reviewer").

Fix direction: skip the rider for role:"reviewer" spawns — check the resolved role before computing/appending the rider (reviewer task passes through byte-identical). Keep it for unrestricted sub-agents (the rider's original purpose: seed a worker's task with prior knowledge). Consider whether the skip should be role-based only or also exposed as an explicit spawn option; document the decision in the rider's comment.

Acceptance criteria: a role:"reviewer" spawn's task reaches the spawner byte-identical to the `task` argument even when the memory store has matching hits; a non-reviewer spawn still gets the rider (existing behavior preserved); a unit test in src/tool/agent/spawn_agent.rs with a memory fixture that has a matching hit asserts the reviewer task stays clean while a normal spawn's task carries the rider; cargo test green + warning-free (#![deny(warnings)]).

text:
Reduce the 1.4MB request body / prefill cost (L4)

Problem (2027-01-09 perf review — LOW as a comms finding but the #1 end-to-end latency lever): the dominant per-turn cost is server-side prefill of the ~1.4MB request body on the uncached prefix — connect_ms 47-86s on the biggest turns (503-message conversations, ~340K-token prompts). Every turn re-pays prefill on whatever is uncached; the client-side share (build + clone + serialize) is only ~25-60ms plus raw upload. The perf report's in-app mitigation levers: compaction aggressiveness (summarize_at, keep_recent) and tool-result truncation (keep_high=20, summary_chars) — which trade the information loss of truncation against this latency.

Fix instructions:
1. Compaction aggressiveness for long sessions: evaluate lowering summarize_at_fill_rate further (0.3 today) or keep_recent for sessions that regularly exceed ~200K — each compaction trades one cold request + summarizer cost for a smaller stable prefix afterward. Measure with the R21 stats (summarizer rows) before/after.
2. Tool-schema pruning with a CACHE CAVEAT: 25 tool schemas ride in the stable head and are cached after the first request — pruning them mid-session would RESET the prefix cache (a new head = full re-bill). Only change the head at session start (e.g. plan-scoped tool sets chosen when the session begins), never mid-conversation.
3. Keep the CONTEXT_FOOTER stable-prefix discipline (already present) — any footer content that changes per iteration defeats the head cache.
4. Coordinate with the 340K cliff item (211e215e): the send-gate + trigger margin there also caps the worst-case prefill.
5. Tests: compaction behavior tests stay green; if plan-scoped tool sets are implemented, a test asserting the head is stable within a session and only varies across sessions/plans.

Acceptance: long-session turns show smaller prompt sizes in request_stats (avgP trend) without a hit-rate regression on reporting models; cargo test --workspace green.

Sandbox: close the hardlink / 8.3-alias / ladder-fallback path-protection bypasses

THREE pre-existing ways to defeat Sandbox's path-prefix write protection, all found during review rounds 2-4 of plan ee65fd4b (2027-01-11, reports .coding/reviews/2026-09-14-research-artifacts-subplan-review-round2.md §Q5 and …-round4.md §Q5; BUG memory recorded). None was fixed there — they predate that change and are broader than it.

(1) HARDLINKS — the dangerous one. canonicalize cannot see a hardlink (no link to follow; the path IS the file), so `.coding/x.toml` hardlinked to `.coding/safety.toml` (or memory.db / plans / reviews / knowledge) is NOT protected by name and is writable by ANY plan kind, truncating the shared inode; `.coding/x.rs` hardlinked to `src/lib.rs` does the same for source. Fix direction: detect it — compare `std::fs::metadata(path)`'s (dev, ino) / Windows file index against the protected set, or refuse when the target path's metadata link count > 1 and the path is inside .coding/ (fail-closed variant acceptable: refuse nlink>1 inside .coding/).

(2) Win32 8.3 SHORT-NAME ALIASES. is_protected_write_target (src/tool/agent/sandbox.rs) trims case + trailing dots/spaces per component but not 8.3 aliases, so `.coding/KNOWLED~1/new/x.md` (knowledge = 9 chars gets an alias; plans/reviews/.git fit 8.3 and get none) reads as ordinary → allowed; validate_for_write step 4 `create_dir_all` resolves the alias and plants a new subtree inside the real .coding/knowledge/. Check whether the volume even generates aliases: `fsutil 8dot3name query C:` or `dir /x .coding`. Fix direction: re-run is_protected_write_target on step 5's CANONICAL result in validate_for_write, not only on its lexical input.

(3) LADDER STEP-5 LEXICAL FALLBACK. validate_for_write (src/tool/agent/sandbox.rs, steps 1-5) returns the LEXICAL path when the final revalidation fails, so a write through a link that escapes the root lands outside it. Reachable for implementation/bug_fixing plans (the research route was closed by plan ee65fd4b). DISCUSSION ITEM (filed 2027-01-14 at the user's request, during plan 987fef4c) — agree the fix approach BEFORE implementing; the acceptance list below is the design target to settle.

SYMPTOM: calling memory_amend with a paragraph that itself opens with "Amended 2027-01-14 …" produced a doubled, contradictory heading in the knowledge file:
  "Amended 2027-01-11: Amended 2027-01-14: the zero-file hint's wording changed …"

text:
file_edit failure classes: line-range pairing, quote-safety, escape-normalization fallback

Problem (observed 2027-01-24, wt/mnemo topology work): repeated file_edit failures from three distinct causes, all fixable:
(1) Line-range mode omitted one of the pair — an edit passed start_line without end_line → "must both be set". The schema lists them as two independent optional fields, so nothing forces them to co-occur.
(2) The apostrophe trap (highest frequency): old_string containing ' fails byte-exact matching when the file has \' (JS-escaped) — failed twice. Class: ' in prose, \ in paths, CRLF vs LF.
(3) No-op / malformed batch items: one edit with old_string === new_string (generic "identical" error), twice an empty argument object on shell/read_files calls.

Fix direction (priority order), all in src/tool/agent/file_edit.rs (tool definition + validation; the advertised schema flows through ToolRegistry::schemas, src/tool/mod.rs):
A. Replace start_line+end_line with a single lines: [start, end] tuple parameter (schema change) — one required tuple cannot be half-filled; kills cause (1).
B. Add a quote-safety pre-flight line to the tool description: "old_string must match byte-exact: JS-escaped apostrophes (\'), backslashes (\\), and line endings are literal. If the anchor contains a quote, a backslash, or is >3 lines, prefer line-range mode."
C. Auto-fallback instead of hard-fail: when a literal old_string misses but matches under (i) unescaping \'→' or (ii) whitespace normalization, apply that match and return a note "matched via escape-normalization" instead of erroring (fuzzy_whitespace exists but does not cover escape differences) — absorbs cause (2), the single biggest win.
D. Reject old_string === new_string at schema validation with "no-op edit: old_string equals new_string", and on a miss echo the first differing byte position ("matched 214/215 chars; first difference at char 41: file has \\', you sent '") — turns a retry loop into a one-shot fix.

Acceptance criteria: cargo test green and warning-free; new unit tests in src/tool/agent/file_edit.rs covering: half-filled line-range impossible/rejected at schema level, escape-normalization fallback applies + notes, no-op edit rejected with the clear message, miss error carries the first-difference pointer.

Related memories: HOW efad709f (large file_edit payloads can silently write empty — chunk them), HOW 0af9a3a2 (retry malformed tool calls immediately), PLAN 4fa222cc (repeat-failure circuit breaker — these failures are the class it catches).

(B) Quote-safety pre-flight line in the schema description + module doc. (C) Escape-normalization fallback in literal_splice (unescaped/escaped variants + whitespace normalization on miss) with a never-silent success NOTE; batch items get per-item notes. text:
Malformed-JSON retry loop: escaped-regex search patterns repeatedly fail to emit

Symptom (observed 2026-09-21, live incident): during a macOS-CI-diagnostic session, the assistant repeatedly failed to emit valid `search` / `search_read` tool-call arguments whenever the `pattern` field contained an escaped-regex construct such as `\(\?<` (matching the literal `(?<`). Each attempt was rejected by the transport with "arguments malformed or truncated — not run; retrying" — 5 consecutive failures in a row — before a paren-free reformulation (`[(][?]`) finally succeeded. The retry loop burned turns and produced no progress; the harness also emits a self-correction note telling the agent to re-emit the COMPLETE call, which the agent did, reproducing the identical failure.

Reproduction: in any session, call the `search` tool with `glob` set and a `pattern` whose JSON encoding requires backslash escapes around regex metacharacters, e.g. {"glob":"static/**","pattern":"\\(\\?<"}. Note this is a *content-emission* failure — the JSON body never reaches the tool, so it is not a regex-validity rejection.

Root cause (suspected, unconfirmed): the model's tool-call argument emission degrades on backslash-dense JSON string values, likely a generation-time escaping interaction (each `\\` and `\"` in the payload compounds). Related precedent in memory: PLAN 4fa222cc "Tool-call robustness: repeat-failure circuit breaker + schema injection" (MERGED into main 8b2ee81) fixed the *downstream* symptom of repeated malformed calls via a circuit breaker + schema re-injection, but it did not address the emission itself. See also DECISION c9bb3a5f (MAX_BAD_JSON_RETRIES=8) and HOW 0af9a3a2 (retry malformed tool calls immediately).

Fix direction: (1) when the retry count for a single tool call exceeds ~3, the harness should surface a distinct, actionable error suggesting the agent reformulate the *argument content* (not merely re-emit), e.g. by using a literal/paren-free regex, `literal: true`, or a glob-only search; (2) consider a `search`-tool ergonomic: accept a `pattern_literal`/`literal: true` path that avoids backslash escaping entirely, and document in the tool description that metacharacter-dense patterns should use `literal: true`; (3) evaluate whether the existing bad-JSON correction message (src/agent/, the correction/schema-injection path from plan a04da1a3) should detect a *repeat* of the same bad-JSON signature and change strategy rather than re-injecting the same schema.

Acceptance criteria: (a) a backslash-dense search pattern that fails twice triggers a differentiated harness message proposing a literal/reformulated pattern rather than a third identical retry; (b) a regression test asserts that two identical bad-JSON failures for the same tool produce a strategy-changing correction (extend the existing repeat-failure tests in src/agent/dispatch.rs / src/agent/tests.rs around `repeat_failure_injects_schema_correction_on_second_identical_error`); (c) `cargo test --workspace` green and warning-free.

Pointers: memory PLAN 4fa222cc (tool-call robustness, merged 8b2ee81), DECISION ab56df6d (repeat-failure circuit breaker), DECISION c9bb3a5f (MAX_BAD_JSON_RETRIES), HOW 0af9a3a2 (retry immediately with corrected params). Live incident occurred during plan 263a9e31 (macOS CI diagnostic) while scanning static/** for `(?<` regex precedents.

text:
Add a status op to git_read (or route it to the git tool)

Problem (observed 2026-09-21, during plan 263a9e31 while checking the tree before the macOS diagnostic dispatch): the `git_read` tool exposes only op=diff/log/show — there is NO status op. Calling git_read with op:"status" fails with `unknown op 'status' — valid: diff, log, show`, and the agent then repeatedly re-emitted the same invalid call, burning turns in a read-loop before falling back to the `git` tool (subcommand:"status"). (2) Sharpen the error text for an unknown op to name the intended alternative explicitly, e.g. `unknown op 'status' — valid: diff, log, show (for working-tree status use the git tool with subcommand:"status")` — the current message lists the valid ops but does not point at the substitute, which is what let the loop persist. (3) Add a regression test asserting op="status" returns short-status output for a dirty tree and empty output for a clean one, and that an unknown op's error names the substitute.

Acceptance criteria: git_read op="status" returns the short-status form (clean tree → empty); the unknown-op error names the working alternative; the tool stays read-only (never mutates the index or fetches); cargo test --workspace green and warning-free; the tool's schema description documents the new op.

text:
Tool correction must change STRATEGY on a repeated bad-JSON signature, not re-inject the schema

Problem (observed live 2026-09-21, plan 263a9e31): the harness already has three mitigations from the earlier robustness work — MAX_BAD_JSON_RETRIES=8 (src/agent/mod.rs:59), the repeat-failure circuit breaker (src/agent/turn.rs::repeated_tool_failure:3470, called from execute_tool_batch:1302), and a schema re-injection correction. All three fired during this session's ~12 malformed-argument calls, but they RE-INJECT THE SCHEMA rather than changing strategy. When the underlying failure is escaping fragility (a backslash-dense JSON string value degrading during generation), the schema is not the missing information — a fourth identical attempt is guaranteed to fail identically. This session burned 5 consecutive attempts on one `search` pattern before a hand-found reformulation ([(][?] instead of the escaped (?<) succeeded.

The diagnostic signal is available and cheap: a repeat of the SAME (tool name, bad-JSON signature) pair distinguishes "the model does not know the schema" (where re-injection is right) from "the argument body failed to emit" (where re-injection is useless). Today both get the same correction.

Fix direction, in the repeat-failure correction path (src/agent/turn.rs — the correction assembly around repeated_tool_failure + the correction/schema-injection site; confirm the exact fn before editing):
1. When a failed tool result's (tool, error text) matches a PRIOR identical bad-JSON failure for the same tool, emit a STRATEGY-CHANGING correction instead of the schema. The text should say the argument body is failing to emit and direct a DIFFERENT formulation, e.g. for search/search_read: "use literal: true, or a pattern free of regex metacharacters"; for any tool: "rebuild the complete argument object from scratch rather than editing the previous one."
2. Keep the existing schema re-injection for the FIRST failure (schema-knowledge class) — do not regress that path.
3. Distinguish the two classes explicitly in the correction builder (a bad-JSON repeat vs an ordinary repeated tool error) — the circuit breaker currently treats them alike.

text:

Why this matters: any pattern containing regex metacharacters (`(?<`, `\d`, `\\`) forces the model to emit a JSON string dense with backslashes, which is exactly the emission class that degrades (see backlog a015d2f7 for the general mechanism). 1. Document `literal: true` in the `pattern` description as the recommended form for text containing regex metacharacters or backslashes, e.g. "For a pattern with regex metacharacters, prefer literal: true — it avoids escaping."
2. State the recovery rule inline, mirroring the read_files fix (backlog 26cdbaf8): "If a call is rejected as malformed, do NOT resend — reformulate with literal: true or a metacharacter-free pattern."
3. Add one inline example of a literal search call so the shape is unambiguous.
4. Consider whether search_read should expose the same `literal` flag for parity (verify it currently does).

text:
Repetition guard: same-batch calls must not trip it; trip = same error across 3 interactions

Problem (user report, 2027-01-24 session): a turn aborted with "repetition guard: 3 identical consecutive responses — breaking the tool loop" (src/agent/turn.rs:738-790, error text at :777). User's intended semantics: three identical tool calls issued AT THE SAME TIME (within one assistant response / one parallel batch) must NOT break the loop; the guard should only break when the SAME error has occurred across three DIFFERENT LLM interactions — the model must get a chance to repair in between (each interaction sees the previous tool result/error before re-emitting).

Current mechanics: one signature per assistant response (text + all tool calls name:arguments joined with \u{1e}, provider ids excluded) pushed into a ring of 3 (turn.rs:749-764); trips when all three sigs are equal (:765-790); ring cleared when tool_error_count > 0 (:758-760); MAX_RETRIES=3 consecutive abort owns the error-retry path (:858).

Investigate first (pull the incident's trace/provider-errors rows): (a) did the trip involve responses whose batch contained duplicate identical calls — the sig joins the whole batch, so three responses each carrying the same 3-call batch trip even though each batch is one moment; (b) did the calls fail with errors that did NOT increment tool_error_count (e.g. tool returned Ok with error text in its output) so the ring-clear at :758-760 never fired and legitimate repair retries were counted as repetition?

Fix direction: make the guard interaction-aware — (1) a batch of identical calls within ONE response is one interaction and must not accumulate toward a trip by itself; (2) trip only when the identical responses were each followed by the same error outcome across three distinct LLM round-trips (model saw the error and still re-emitted byte-identical work = genuine loop); (3) verify the tool_error_count clear covers every error shape (failed execution vs error-text-as-success-output) so a repairing model is never counted.

Acceptance criteria: regression tests in src/agent/tests.rs — one response with 3 identical calls never trips nor poisons the ring; the same failing call re-emitted across three interactions with the same error each time trips (or is owned by MAX_RETRIES — decide per investigation and document); a model that changes args after an error never trips. cargo test green + warning-free. Update the contract text in docs/FEATURES.md:54.

Pointers: BUG memory .coding/knowledge/bug/2027-01-07-cross-turn-re-emission-tool-loop-pattern-continu.md (guard origin, plan 70d2283d); review rounds pinning guard-B semantics .coding/reviews/2026-09-07-70d2283d-compaction-bound-round2/3/4.md.

kNN overlay classifier for failure triage — genuinely online learning (item 4b)

text:
Content index: reindex stale files above the 8-file cap (adaptive budget, not a hard count)

Observed live 2027-01-25 in the Mnemo repo: a `search` for "AgentLoop {" returned "note: content index stale for 9 file(s) — serving tree-walk results" — NINE stale files, one over the inline-repair cap, so the query fell back to the walk. So the user-visible complaint "it should reindex the stale items instead of warning" is ALREADY 90% shipped — the gap is exactly the >8 case. Note the files were stale from the normal edit→watcher lag (several files edited moments earlier by file tools; multi_edit is not special — the watcher reindexes on its own pass, and the per-query check compares each hit file's on-disk mtime against the as-of-index mtime).

PROBLEM: Capability gap vs alexgreensh/token-optimizer (2.4k stars; audited 2026-09 from README + BENCHMARK.md). Their thesis matches our own cache-hit analysis: command-output compression is only 15-25% of context waste; the rest is re-reads, compaction loss, and behavior. Mnemo covers the boundary (compaction, truncation, cache split) but not the contents. What exists today: compaction src/agent/context.rs::mechanical_compaction + src/agent/turn.rs::maybe_compact:1929 + src/runtime/agent.rs::compact_context:1103; lossy tail truncation src/agent/context.rs::truncate_tool_result_at:829 and truncate_to_token_budget:1591; prompt-cache stable-head split; telemetry src/memory/mod.rs::record_request_stats:2062; UI frontend/src/components/chat/InflightBar.tsx (ctx popup) + frontend/src/components/views/StatsView.tsx.

1. Delta + skeleton re-reads: src/tool/agent/read_files.rs serves full content on every call, though most reads are re-reads of files already in context. Serve diff-only when the file changed, signature/import skeleton when unchanged, full content on first read.
2. Semantic command-output compression: collapse cargo/npm/pytest/build/lint output to distinct error lines + counts + exit status, credential-safe, with a user-extensible allowlist. Truncation today cuts arbitrary tails with no semantics.
3. Progressive disclosure: archive full originals (over a size cap) to disk with preview + expand retrieval (FTS5 search over the archive); today truncated tails are lost forever. Net re-expansions subtract from savings.
4. Compaction survival: pre-compaction checkpoints at fill thresholds + restore after; decision extraction (cap ~10, injected as must-preserve at compaction time); heuristic post-compaction digest (files touched, errors seen, line counts, no LLM call). Today: one summarize shot + mechanical fallback — a lossy summary loses everything with no recovery.
5. Savings ledger: SQLite per-event before/after token counts, metered vs estimated kept separate — the metering foundation for all levers above and the dashboard.
6. Quality score: S-F grade computed from fill %, waste tokens, stale-read rate, decision density; surfaced in the InflightBar ctx popup; nudge on significant drop (with cooldown).
7. Lean-output nudge: cache-safe injected note at >25% fill steering concise visible output (output tokens cost ~5x input).
8. Dashboard upgrade: per-turn token drill-down, cache hit-rate/TTL analysis, savings tracker, quality overlay, per-feature toggles — extend frontend/src/components/views/StatsView.tsx.

FIX DIRECTION: implement natively in the tool dispatch layer + src/agent/context.rs — we own the layer, so no hook processes: typed events, real tests. Invariants: never mutate the already-sent prefix (protects the prompt-cache split); archive before substituting, fail-open on archive errors; every feature behind a flag, default off until A/B-measured on our own sessions.

Nothing is mechanically enforced, so cost depends on the dispatching agent's discipline.

FIX DIRECTION — deterministic in the app, not a convention:
(1) DELTA-SCOPED ROUNDS. A re-review (reviewer spawn while a prior report exists for the plan) must get a mechanically-derived base: when a report lands, stamp the reviewed tree state — extend write_review_report (src/tool/agent/write_review_report.rs) plus the `last_review_report` tracking (src/agent/loop_impl.rs:1073-1091) to record the reviewed commit-ish in the report front matter and on the plan frame — then render the re-review preamble from it: "state verified as of <ref>; `git diff <ref>` is your scope — verify ONLY those hunks; the rest was verified and is unchanged." text:
Make file_edit's ops path as resilient as multi_edit (false "emission artifact" rejections)

Observed 2027-01-16 on wt/mnemo (plan 2f74e10a, step "main.rs + rewire.rs"), editing src-tauri/src/main.rs around lines 1404-1460 (a `match (mode, enabled)` → `if enabled` restructure plus a 4-space dedent). file_edit rejected FOUR different calls with the identical error, while multi_edit accepted a strictly larger one on the same region/file minutes later.

EXACT ERROR (src/tool/agent/edit_ops.rs:186 + :199):
"invalid input: edit rejected: emission artifact detected (unbalanced delimiters after the edit (the brace/bracket/paren deficit grew) — the truncation artifact: the payload was cut off) — the payload looks corrupted (model emission decay; see .coding/knowledge/bug/2026-12-20-code-bearing-tool-payload-emissions-degrade-unde.md). Do not blind-retry: re-emit carefully in SMALLER fragments, or use file_write for full-file replacement. (This is not a content-drift failure — a re-read will not help.)"

REPRO / EVIDENCE (all on src-tauri/src/main.rs, same session):
- REJECTED file_edit ops [2 anchor objects, ~3.2 KB total; one op rewrites `let managed_classifier = match (` → `let x = if enabled {` = 1 paren-open becomes 1 brace-open]
- REJECTED file_edit ops [1 anchor object ~1.5 KB; same +1-brace conversion]
- REJECTED file_edit lines:[1428,1460] (line-range mode, ~1.4 KB new_string, dedent only)
- REJECTED file_edit ops [10 compact line ops, ~700 B; included `r1451:    } else {` replacing a bare `}` → call delta +1]
- ACCEPTED file_edit ops [same 10 ops PLUS `d1417` (a line that opened a brace) → call delta 0, ~250 B]
- ACCEPTED multi_edit files:[{path: src-tauri/src/main.rs, ops:[20 compact ops, ~1.6 KB]}] — 6x the payload, 2x the ops of the rejected file_edit call
=> The discriminator is the CALL's net delimiter delta, not payload size; multi_edit does not apply (or applies a weaker) version of the same rule. Workaround cost ~10 extra round-trips and forced per-line re-indents with hand-paired compensating deletions.

FIX DIRECTION (smallest sufficient):
1. Unify the payload-assembly + artifact-guard path so file_edit (src/tool/agent/file_edit.rs) and multi_edit (src/tool/agent/multi_edit.rs) get IDENTICAL behaviour — the shared guard lives in src/tool/agent/edit_ops.rs.
2. Make the guard balance-aware: compute the applied ops' net delta and compare it against the FILE's actual brace/paren/bracket balance, instead of treating a positive fragment delta as truncation. Legitimate edits open blocks (`match (a,b) { arm => {` → `if a { if b {`).
3. When delta > 0 stays suspicious, accept it if the call also carries compensating ops; otherwise name the offending op IN THE ERROR (index + its delta, e.g. "op 5 grows the brace balance by 1") so the agent can rebalance instead of guessing/splitting.
4. Provide an explicit escape hatch (e.g. `artifact_check: false`, approval-gated) for when the agent can verify the result itself (`rustfmt --check <file>` / `cargo check`).

- The four rejected call shapes above apply as-is (or fail with the explicit offending-op delta message).
- A file_edit ops call at ~1.6 KB / 20 ops with net-zero delta succeeds, matching the accepted multi_edit call.
- New unit tests in src/tool/agent/edit_ops.rs: (i) `}`→`} else {` paired with a compensating deletion → applied; (ii) the same op alone → applied or an actionable per-op error (pick and document one); (iii) a genuinely truncated/unbalanced payload → still rejected.
VERIFY: `cargo test edit_ops`, `cargo test multi_edit`, then full root `cargo test` (warning-free — both crate roots are #![deny(warnings)]).

text:
create_plan: record probe evidence, not assumptions

Observed 2027-01-11 during a browser/ShapeGraph planning run: a plan is authored on assumed facts, step 1 discovers the assumption is false, and the whole plan must be rewritten before any code is written. Three concrete cases from that one session:
1. Unverified reachability — the plan assumed ext._evaluator.clashOf() was callable from /agent.html. It was not: the ShapeGraph extension is never loaded on that page (typeof ext._evaluator -> "undefined"). One 30-second live probe would have caught it before ~4,600 characters of context were written.
2. Wrong file targeted from a name match — clash exists at static/scripts/shapegraph/tools.js:862, which looks like the right home, but it belongs to a different page's tool layer. Name similarity is not reachability.
3. Stale counts asserted as fact — "108 solids" came from _doc.solids while _shapes held 192 frag entries; the two are not 1:1, so any loop written against the wrong one is wrong.

Root cause: the plan encodes assumptions as if they were findings. NOTE the tooling did not misfire — the resumability-gate rejection seen in that session (a step naming no file path) was the gate doing its job correctly; do not weaken it.

Fix direction: do reachability probes at PLANNING time and write results into the plan context as verified facts with the evidence attached — e.g. "Probe on the live page: typeof ext._evaluator -> undefined; ShapeGraph ext never loaded there" survives step 1, whereas an inferred "ext._evaluator.clashOf() handles the whole-model scan" does not. A first step whose content is only "verify X" is legitimate ONLY when X is genuinely un-probeable without writing code; otherwise the probe belongs in planning. Candidate enforcement lever: the gate requires any context line asserting a symbol exists / is callable to carry an evidence marker (e.g. "verified:"), with assumption lines explicitly labelled.

Touch points: src/tool/workflow/plan.rs — CreatePlanTool (:471), its schema/description text (:546), the pure validator (:2346) and the tool-level resumability gate (:3426); src/agent/factory.rs prompt/tool-description byte baselines (:2119, :2210, :2366, :2434, :2498) must be updated in the same commit if the description text changes.

Acceptance: (a) guidance/tool description distinguishes assumption from verified-with-evidence; (b) a unit test in src/tool/workflow/plan.rs proves the gate flags an unevidenced reachability claim and accepts an evidenced one; (c) all existing resumability-gate tests stay green; (d) schema-doc baselines in src/agent/factory.rs updated in the same commit.

Image tools hidden in Planning and Complete

The image_* family (image_analysis, image_ui_diff, image_diff, ...) is invisible in the Planning and Complete workflow states, but those tools are READ-ONLY w.r.t. the project and are needed while planning — e.g. a plan that must account for an attached screenshot or design mockup cannot look at the image before a plan exists.

SYMPTOM (how to reproduce): from Complete or Planning, the tool list carries no image_* entry. Root cause, verified by reading the code: src/tool/mod.rs ToolFilter::allows() — the Planning arm (line ~583) and the Complete arm (line ~807) both gate ToolCategory::Agent to `(safety == SafetyLevel::AutoRun && !name.starts_with("mcp__")) || name == "spawn_agent"`. Every image tool in src/tool/agent/image_tools/tools.rs is ToolCategory::Agent (tools.rs:700, the ImageAnalysisTool impl) and reports `fn safety(&self) -> SafetyLevel { SafetyLevel::NeedsApproval }` (tools.rs:718), so both arms deny it. The family never mutates project files — it reads an image and calls the vision model — so the "no changes without a plan" rule does not justify hiding it; only the approval prompt does, and that prompt is orthogonal to state visibility (exactly the argument the Browser tools use at src/tool/mod.rs:615-622 and 811-817). Each image tool also sets `fn deferred_group(&self) -> Option<&'static str> { Some("image") }` (tools.rs:706), so the family is already tagged.

FIX DIRECTION (plan it): make the image family visible in Planning + Complete. Minimal, in-style option: name-gate the family in BOTH Agent arms of ToolFilter::allows() the same way spawn_agent already is — `|| name.starts_with("image_")` in the Planning arm (~line 583) and the Complete arm (~line 807). KEEP SafetyLevel::NeedsApproval so each call still prompts; do NOT relax the safety level to AutoRun, which would silently drop the approval prompt in Executing too. Alternative if name-matching the family is unwanted: add a trait-level read-only marker on Tool (e.g. `fn reads_only_project(&self) -> bool` defaulting to false) and consult it in both arms — prefer whichever option can be covered by a test that enumerates the REAL registered tool list rather than a hardcoded name list. Do not change the Reviewer or Skill arm behaviour.

ACCEPTANCE: (1) a test in src/tool/mod.rs beside the existing per-state availability tests (~lines 2316-2440, e.g. skill_create_is_executing_only_unless_a_skill_names_it) asserting every registered image_* tool is allowed under ToolFilter::Planning AND ToolFilter::Complete, while mutating Agent tools (file_edit, file_write, shell, git) stay DENIED in those two states — the plan-first hard rule must survive; (2) `cargo test` green and warning-free (the crate roots are #![deny(warnings)]); (3) if the Planning/Complete tool surface is described in docs/FEATURES.md or agent.md, update that text.

VERIFY: `cargo test` unpiped and read its result lines (never trust a piped exit code). Then confirm in-app that from Complete the image tools appear and that each call still prompts for approval.

Problem (user-reported this session; the SECOND live report on this warning — the first, 2027-01-15 "it had switched away", is recorded in SPEC .coding/knowledge/spec/2027-01-11-same-project-instance-warning-is-a-launch-time-s.md): closing mnemo down does not clean up the "another instance of mnemo is running on this project" warning. Repro: (1) launch instance A on a project, launch instance B on the same project (B shows the warning dialog); close A — B's dialog stays on screen, still claiming an instance is working on the project; (2) on clean exit nothing removes <project>/.coding/instance.json, so a stale marker can later warn again when Windows recycles the dead pid to a live process.

Root cause (per the SPEC): <project>/.coding/instance.json {pid, started_at} is written ONLY at launch (src-tauri/src/main.rs:328-344; sole writer InstanceMarker::write src-tauri/src/instance_marker.rs:49) — nothing clears or updates it on app exit or project switch-away. The conflict is computed ONCE at startup (conflict_for src-tauri/src/instance_marker.rs:69 + instance_pid_alive src-tauri/src/startup.rs:115) -> runtime ctx (src-tauri/src/ipc/state.rs:155) -> StartupSnapshot -> frontend state (frontend/src/App.tsx:261); the dialog (App.tsx:731) renders while non-null, never re-evaluated, never retracted. It warns, does not lock.

Fix direction: (1) src-tauri: on clean exit (app exit + the project-switch restart path src-tauri/src/ipc/projects.rs:201) remove <project>/.coding/instance.json ONLY when the stored marker still names this process (read_marker + pid == std::process::id() guard before delete — last-writer-wins means a newer incumbent must be preserved); best-effort, never block exit; add the removal helper in src-tauri/src/instance_marker.rs with unit tests in its mod tests. (2) frontend: re-evaluate the conflict while the dialog is visible (liveness re-check on an interval/focus) and retract once the pid is dead; reword the dialog copy to "launched on this project (PID n, HH:MM)" per the SPEC — never assert current occupancy.

Acceptance: closing the warned-about instance retracts the surviving instance's warning without restart; after a clean exit the marker file is gone when the exiting instance was the last writer; crash re-launch still ignores its own stale marker; cargo test green with the new unit tests.
